question.text: The density of the material of a cube can be estimated by measuring its mass and the length of one of its sides. If the maximum error in the measurement of mass and length are $0.3 \%$ and $0.2 \%$ respectively, the maximum error in the estimation of the density of the cube is approximately.

solution.text:
Given,
Maximum error in the measurement of mass $=0.3 \%$
Maximum error in the measurement of length $=0.2 \%$
We know that,
Error in density is given as,
$\text {Density, } \rho=\frac{\text { mass }(m)}{\text { volume }(V)}=\frac{m}{L^{3}}$
where, $L=$ side of cube
Error in density is given as,
$\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right)=\frac{\Delta m}{m}+\frac{3 \Delta L}{L}$
or $\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right) \times 100=\left(\frac{\Delta m}{m}+\frac{3 \Delta L}{L}\right) \times 100$
Substituting the given values, we get
$\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right)_{\max }=(0.3 \%+3(0.2) \%=0.3 \%+0.6 \%$
$\therefore$ Maximum percentage error measurement of density $\left(\frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho}\right)_{\max }=0.9 \%$
